summary: Friedberg argues that Google's AlphaFold 3, kept proprietary inside Isomorphic Labs, represents an extraordinary competitive asset that could generate $100B+ in value from drug discovery, giving Alphabet a massive, underappreciated portfolio bet in bioengineering that is now commercially locked up.
quote: I think Google's got this like portfolio of like quiet, extraordinarily high bets... the fact that they didn't open source everything in this says a lot about their intentions.

summary: Chamath argues Apple has too much capital and too few ideas, missed strategic opportunities (Tesla, car, gaming), and cannot execute large M&A — signaling a company with deteriorating growth prospects despite its enormous cash position.
quote: There are just too many examples here where these guys have so much money and not enough ideas. That's a shame... it goes back to a complete lack of will.

summary: Chamath views OpenAI as one of four major companies that will matter in AI, with its durable value coming not just from the model but from the surrounding infrastructure and scaffolding that customers will pay for — analogous to AWS for open-source software.
quote: I think that these guys are going to be one of the four major companies that matter in this whole space... the models will basically be all really good. And then it's all this other stuff that you'll have to pay for.
